metadata.case_name: NG KA HO v. YEUNG KWOK LEUNG

injuries.description: head injury without loss of consciousness
source: The Plaintiff sustained head injury without loss of consciousness.
He also had right knee pain and laceration near the right eyebrow. The laceration was sutured.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of eyelid or periocular area

source: He also had right knee pain and laceration near the right eyebrow.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg, unspecified

injuries.description: mild post-concussional syndrome with residual giddiness and subjective memory loss
source: Dr. Edmund Woo ... opined that there was mild post-concussional syndrome with residual giddiness and subjective memory loss.
The diagnosis was ‘Pervasive Developmental Disorder Unspecified’.

injuries.description: aggravation of the symptoms of Pervasive Developmental Disorder by the accident
source: Having considered the above, I accept Dr. Chung’s analysis that the existing condition of the Plaintiff was a progression of the Plaintiff’s PDD. It was aggravated by the accident and other stress.

injuries.description: mild residual symptoms of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder / post-traumatic distress symptoms
source: Both of them found that the Plaintiff suffered from mild residual symptoms of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder.
Both Dr. Wong and Dr. Chung agreed that the Plaintiff suffered from mild symptoms of Post Traumatic Distress Symptoms.

manifestations.description: dizziness
vomiting
residual giddiness
subjective memory loss / loss of memory
headache (noted when studying)
nightmares about the accident (first one and half years)
fear / afraid of crossing a road by himself; anxiety when crossing roads and taking transport
repeated hand washing (frequent washing of hands)
long showers / taking showers for over an hour (later 30 minutes)
shutting/slamming doors forcibly
meticulous checking of school bag before bed
scratching head repeatedly
phobia of height / refused to take lift with transparent walls
saying the same thing or asking the same question repeatedly; self-muttering; smiling to himself
hitting walls and kicking tables (about 3 times a month around 2002-2003)
reduced interpersonal skill / lack of normal reciprocal social interaction and communication; difficulty communicating with peers
delayed language development milestone
restricted social contact / compromised relationship with peers / bullied by classmates
irritability and temper tantrums
deterioration (or change) in academic results (disputed as to cause)

treatments_received: admission to Neurosurgery unit (Prince of Wales Hospital) and follow-up in Neurosurgery and Paediatrics Units until 23rd December 1999
X-ray and Computerized Tomography Scan of the brain
psychiatric medication (mother reported improvement after taking medication from the psychiatrist)
recommendation to attend Assertiveness Training Group (clinical psychologist)
treatments_future: intensive treatment program for 18 months involving clinical psychologist and child psychiatrist (recommended by Dr. Wong)

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Fear of crossing roads by himself, anxiety when crossing roads and taking transport; nightmares about the accident
Compromised relationship with peers, restricted social contact and bullying resulting in reduced social interaction
Subjective memory loss and related cognitive complaints following the accident
Reduced earning capacity / limitation to clerical level employment as a result of the aggravated condition

comparable_cases.injury_description: 13-year-old girl hit by a collapsed canopy; superficial injuries; frequent nightmares and fear of darkness; impairment in psychological and social functioning; needed intensive psychotherapy
moderate degree of PTSD and depressive disorder after an assault in which his head was thrown against a wall
